newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FCC has busy agenda next week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FCC has busy agenda next week.

text.p: The Federal Communications Commission is expected to complete work next week on several key rules and proposals covering such topics as advanced digital television, access charge reform and international accounting rates, FCC officials said Friday.
The agency is expected to approve final rules governing a broadcast standard for a new generation of high-definition digital television.
"We want to vote it next week," FCC Chairman Reed Hundt told a news conference. The move follows an agreement reached last month between the computer and TV industries covering a proposed standard.
The agency's proposal to reform the access charges that long-distance carriers pay local phone companies to connect to their network is expected to go out for public comment.
FCC officials say privately the plan is unlikely to contain many conclusions but rather will ask questions about differing approaches to reforming the system.
The agency also is set to unveil its proposal designed to reduce the rates that U.S. carriers pay state-run foreign monopolies to complete overseas calls.

The FCC proposal is expected to set "benchmark" rates for what U.S. carriers could pay foreign carriers to terminate calls. The idea is to drive these "accounting rates" closer to the actual costs of completing a call.
FCC officials say the accounting rates run five to 10 times actual costs, reflecting the power of state-run monopolies unexposed to home competition.

FCC officials recently briefed their overseas counterparts about the proposal, which is likely to ruffle some feathers. The FCC has incorporated some of the overseas comments into the plan, officials said.
"Everybody is waiting to see what we're going to propose," Don Gips, head of the FCC's international bureau, told the press conference.
